text:
sanjay: Heads up — nightly retrieval eval flagged a weird recall dip for the long-tail prompt cohort. not a full outage but noticeable 

eval-bot: nightly-eval | 1959876500
- overall R@10: 0.814 -> 0.781 (-4.1%)
- cohort 'long-tail-guides' R@10: 0.672 -> 0.512 (-23.8%)
- avg reranker score delta: -0.12

ellie: omg that's large for that cohort. any change deployed to reranker or embeddings last night?

kai: we rolled quantized embed candidate (`embed-microq-1`) to staging yesterday afternoon but not to prod. reranker 1.4 had a small weight tweak (beta) in A/B 2 hours before the run.

mia: @sanjay can you paste a couple failing queries + topk results? quick eyeballing helps.

sanjay: sure, sample below (query / top doc ids / reranker scores):
```
Q: "best way to configure db for multi-tenant SaaS"
topk ids: [a23, f91, k11, z55, b08, ...]
before scores: [0.92, 0.89, 0.86, 0.80, 0.78]
after scores:  [0.65, 0.63, 0.60, 0.58, 0.57]
```

jordan: looks like strong score compression across the board. that points to either embedding shift or reranker input distribution change (e.g., tokenization differences).

ellie: I pulled embedding centroids for that cohort. mean cosine to canonical seed dropped ~0.11 for microq embeddings vs baseline fp16. distribution widened. could be quantization artifact.

kai: hmm but we didn't promote microq to prod. are we sure eval used prod index? eval-bot: run environment = prod-index + staging-reranker-config (canary), embed model = fp16 (prod).

mia: OK so embeddings should be stable. reranker canary config could still explain it. who triggered canary? infra-bot: canary-rollout:reranker-1.4 -> 10% @ 1959874800 by kai

ellie: 10% canary could bias nightly if cohorts are routed oddly. what was request routing for nightly job? sanjay: nightly load used uniform bucket - but we set seed change yesterday to randomize queries before sharding. might have increased canary exposure.

jordan: two hypotheses: (A) reranker weight tweak reduced score dynamic range causing recall fall; (B) index dedupe/merge changed doc IDs order leading to different topk and poorer reranking. both plausible.

mia: simple reproducer: run the cohort queries against prod-index but force reranker config to baseline and to canary and compare scores. I can run that in ~15m.

kai: added a quick query diff script:
```
python tools/compare_topk.py --cohort long-tail-guides --reranker baseline --reranker canary --topk 20 --out /tmp/rt.diff
```

ellie: I ran it on a sample of 100 queries. baseline had mean R@10 0.69, canary 0.51. per-query diffs attached in gist: https://rwd.gists/abc123 (private)

sanjay: nice. can you paste an example where baseline returns a high-quality doc that canary demotes?

ellie: pasted one: baseline top1 id=a23 snip: "Multi-tenant DB sharding patterns..." score 0.94; canary top1 id=f91 (less relevant) score 0.64.

jordan: that screams weight scaling. kai, what changed in the canary?

kai: tiny change: increased lexical-sim weight from 0.6 -> 0.7, reduced semantic weight 0.4 -> 0.3 in the combined scorer. intention was to favor exact-match for short queries. seems to harm these long-tail conversational prompts.

mia: ah, cohort is long-form guides where semantics matter more than lexical heuristics. changing weights would majorly impact recall.

jordan: plan: 1) rollback canary to baseline for reranker; 2) re-run nightly eval; 3) create targeted reranker config for long-tail cohort (different weights) or per-route policy.

kai: I can pause rollout (already 10%) and schedule a rollback. infra-bot: rollback scheduled by kai -> reranker-1.4 baseline @ 1959877800

sanjay: also let's add a regression test: nightly eval should include cohort-level checks and fail the rollout if any cohort dips >10% R@10. eval-bot: noted - creating ticket TKT-3192.

mia: also we should log per-query signal like token-length, exact-match ratio, and reranker-feature-distribution to detect future weight sensitivity automatically.

ellie: one more oddity — a small subset of queries showed near-identical embedding centroids but hugely different doc order. could be index shuffling after recent index compaction. infra-bot: index-compact job ran @ 1959873600 for shard 7,8,9

jordan: compaction can change internal doc placement but shouldn't change retrieval scores. still, let's pin index snapshot for eval to avoid silent drift.

kai: agreed. I'll update the rollout playbook: include eval snapshot pin + cohort guardrails.

sanjay: thanks all. action items: kai rollback + update playbook; ellie provide per-query diffs & gist; mia add feature-logging; jordan add cohort gate to nightly eval. I'll follow up in TKT-3192. :thumbsup:

eval-bot: ticket created: TKT-3192 - "Cohort-level R@10 guardrails + reranker rollout safeguards"

mia: marking this as resolved for now — monitor next nightly and report.
